decision: PROMISING narrowly for aligned variable-rank tasks; independent tasks require private intrinsic state
facts: Aligned tasks: Mirror 8,557 B / query NRMSE 3.78e-7; direct adaptive intrinsic 9,110 B / 3.18e-7; generic adaptive PCA 9,352 B / 5.80e-7.
Shared U costs 8,192 B. Mirror task code state is 314 B versus direct 867 B and PCA 1,109 B in aligned stratum.
Aligned active dimension average is 15/32; no private split events.
Independent tasks select full dimension; 23/24 tasks trigger private residual allocation. Mirror+private uses 12,978 B vs direct 9,926 B. No-private Mirror has NRMSE 1.218.
interpretation: Adaptive dimension plus shared Givens view improves total storage by ~6% versus direct adaptive intrinsic coordinates and ~8.5% versus generic PCA for this aligned low-rank task family at near-equal quality. Independent tasks erase the gain and require private state. This is a limited functional feasibility result, not a general intrinsic-learning claim.
hypothesis: Supported narrowly on aligned variable-rank tasks; private residual allocation is necessary for independent task vectors.
counter_hypothesis: The teacher is generated from the same Givens orbit and uses a full-rank anchor to recover the shared vector. The advantage may disappear on learned or shifted task families; total saving is modest because U dominates bytes.
limitations: Random projection basis, not pretrained model
Teacher uses known Givens family and anchor phase
No optimization-based learning of the shared basis or real task quality
